subject: Immediate: CheckoutLabs reserved throughput underrun + GPU pool saturation - CRO briefing requested
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@checkoutlabs.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: CheckoutLabs: 30% below reserved throughput since 0300 PDT, urgent

Hi Lauren,

We started seeing sustained throughput degradation against our reserved commit this morning (~03:15 PDT). Token throughput across our production routes is ~30% below committed capacity and latency p50 has slipped from 120ms to ~380ms. We're also intermittently seeing 5xx errors for inference calls (sampled traces attached). This is impacting payment-authorize flow — we've queued a mitigation on our side but we need Redwood to prioritize.

Can you confirm whether the dedicated GPU pool serving our reservation is saturated, and whether any failover to burst or compatible variants is occurring? Our SLAs rely on committed throughput for peak mornings. If this persists we'll need immediate remediation and a credit discussion — ops are standing by.

Attached: support_trace_20280819.zip (samples + spans).

Best,
Samir
Senior SRE, CheckoutLabs

--
CheckoutLabs | payments at scale

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@checkoutlabs.com>
Date: 2028-08-19T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CheckoutLabs: 30% below reserved throughput since 0300 PDT, urgent

Looping in initial findings from infra quick-check (summary):
- Dedicated pool holo-566 (us-west-2) hosting CheckoutLabs reservation shows 92% GPU util on average across cards for the period 02:45–09:00 PDT; however one node (holo-566-n12) exhibited sustained >98% util and multiple OOM-reclaim spikes between 03:10–04:00.
- KV-cache hit-rate for your most-used route (/v1/pay/authorize) dropped from 78% to 46% after a partial cache invalidation event at 02:50 — this increased per-request compute and amplified GPU pressure.
- Autoscale logs show the pool attempted allocation for burst nodes but was rate-limited due to recent quota reconciliation with the regional scheduler (we hit a staging-to-prod allocation cap). That explains constrained burst.
- 5xx errors in your traces correspond to node-side preemption/rejects when the OOM-reclaim cycle triggered.

Immediate mitigations executed (09:20 PDT):
- Forced draining of holo-566-n12 and restarted the instance to clear kernel-level memory thrash.
- Applied temporary override to regional allocation cap to allow two additional burst instances (expected online in ~6 minutes).
- Replayed core KV-cache priming for top-50 keys for /v1/pay/authorize to recover hit-rate (in progress).

Remaining asks for CheckoutLabs ops:
- Please confirm one failing request-id from your traces (this will let us verify the exact rejection point).
- Share any recent deployment or config that could have triggered cache invalidation (e.g., model version rollout, batching config changes).

I'll continue monitoring and will post updated telemetry. Attaching raw logs: playback_kv_cache_svclog.txt and reserved_capacity_report_2028Q3.pdf.

-David
Director, Production Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: CheckoutLabs: 30% below reserved throughput since 0300 PDT, urgent

Thanks David — we appreciate the quick triage. Failing request-id: chk-req-20280819-30712. Our infra team did a model variant flip earlier this morning (v2.1 -> v2.2) during a quiet window at ~02:30; I can confirm no batching config changes.

We rely on the KV cache to keep p99s stable; if priming is underway, we can help by warming keys from our side. Also — if you foresee material SLA impact >1 hour, we need a formal credit and an interim routing plan.

I'll stand by for the burst node ETA.

Samir
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@checkoutlabs.com>

Subject: Customer update + request for CRO briefing if mitigation not closed in 60m

Quick customer-ready summary: see below — taking this to operations and leadership if unresolved within 60 minutes. Please review and ok to send.

---
Hi Samir,

Short update from Redwood: our infra team identified saturation on a node in your dedicated pool which triggered OOM-driven rejects and temporarily blocked burst allocation due to a regional allocation cap. We forced a node restart, primed KV-cache, and released two additional burst instances; telemetry shows initial recovery but we're still monitoring for p99 impact.

What we need from you: the single failing request-id (you provided chk-req-20280819-30712 — thanks) and confirmation whether you want us to route select heavy paths to a compatible alternative model variant until full KV-cache warm is restored.

If this is not resolved within the hour we'll escalate to the CRO for an exec-level remediation and discuss commercial relief.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
---

Action items for internal ops: David to confirm burst node online time and whether any further pool isolation required; Lauren to prepare an exec brief for CRO and VP Product if we exceed the 60m window.

-Marissa
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@checkoutlabs.com>
Date: 2028-08-20T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: 24h follow-up: Exec summary requested / proposed remediation & credit framework

Team / Samir — quick 24-hour readout and proposal now that we've had a full telemetry pass.

Findings (summary):
- Root cause chain: model variant rollout (v2.1 -> v2.2) caused cache invalidation window which reduced KV cache hit-rate for high-frequency keys; a single degraded node hit sustained >98% GPU util leading to transient OOM reclaim cycles; regional allocation caps prevented immediate burst scale to absorb the delta.
- Impact: CheckoutLabs saw ~28–33% throughput underrun vs reserved commit for 02:50–10:30 PDT; p50 latency normalized after priming but p99 remained elevated for several hours. We correlate the bulk of 5xx rejects to the OOM reclaim window.

Remediation completed/applied:
- Added a permanent regional-scheduler override for CheckoutLabs reservation to increase burst headroom by +2 GPUs during peak windows.
- Implemented an automatic KV-cache soft-prime at variant rollout to avoid a cold-window on model switches.
- Strengthened node health checks to auto-drain nodes before OOM cycles propagate.

Commercial proposal (for discussion):
- Immediate: apply a one-time usage credit equivalent to 8 hours of reserved capacity at committed rate (to offset the reduced deliverable).
- If a repeat outage of this class occurs in the next 90 days, offer an elevated SLA (shorter incident-to-remediation targets) and additional credit framework.

Next steps:
- Samir: confirm that the extra burst headroom and soft-prime are acceptable and whether CheckoutLabs will accept the 8-hour credit as an interim remedy.
- Marissa: I'll need a short paragraph from CS to joint-commit to the customer timeline and credit wording so I can present to CRO.
- David: please attach final telemetry snapshot for the 02:30–11:00 window and confirm persistent mitigations are in prod.

Lauren
Account Executive — Enterprise, Redwood Inference

--
Note: internal/cc'd leadership briefing draft is ready if we do not get acceptance within 6 hours.
